senses.definition: to accept something reluctantly but without protest
senses.example: After a long argument, he acquiesced to their demands.

senses.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly
senses.example: The librarian admonished the boys for talking.

senses.definition: conducive to success; favorable
senses.example: The sunny morning was an auspicious start to the festival.

senses.definition: a person falsely claiming to have a special knowledge or skill
senses.example: The so-called healer turned out to be a charlatan.

senses.definition: having knowledge or being aware of
senses.example: We are cognizant of the risks involved.

senses.definition: feelings of anxiety or dismay, typically at something unexpected
senses.example: To the consternation of his parents, he quit college.

senses.definition: to reduce something in quality or value
senses.example: The coins were debased with cheaper metals.

senses.definition: a division or contrast between two things that are represented as being opposed or entirely different
senses.example: The novel explores the dichotomy between duty and desire.

senses.definition: to cause or give rise to a feeling, situation or condition
senses.example: The policy engendered resentment among farmers.

senses.definition: to destroy completely; to put an end to
senses.example: The vaccine helped eradicate smallpox.

senses.definition: fast and energetic in a rather wild and uncontrolled way
senses.example: The kitchen was a scene of frenetic activity before dinner.

senses.definition: to provoke or annoy someone so as to stimulate an action or reaction
senses.example: His friends goaded him into jumping off the pier.

senses.definition: a person who believes that the pursuit of pleasure is the most important thing in life
senses.example: The hedonist spent his days at parties and his nights at the casino.

senses.definition: acting or done quickly and without thought or care
senses.example: In an impetuous moment, he quit his job.

senses.definition: in an initial stage; beginning to happen or develop
senses.example: The doctor spotted signs of incipient arthritis.

senses.definition: unwilling or unable to believe something
senses.example: She gave him an incredulous look when he claimed he'd cleaned the house.

senses.definition: persisting tirelessly
senses.example: The indefatigable campaigner visited every town in the state.

senses.definition: done at random or without careful judgment
senses.example: The indiscriminate use of antibiotics breeds resistant bacteria.

senses.definition: tending to obstruct or harm
senses.example: High taxes are inimical to growth.

senses.definition: showing a rude and arrogant lack of respect
senses.example: The insolent pupil was sent to the principal.

senses.definition: having, showing or done with good judgment or sense
senses.example: A judicious use of color brightens the room.

senses.definition: existing but not yet developed or manifest; hidden or concealed
senses.example: The tests revealed a latent talent for languages.

senses.definition: not sufficiently strict, severe or careful
senses.example: Security at the depot was lax.

senses.definition: lacking energy or enthusiasm
senses.example: The heat left everyone listless.

senses.definition: a temporary interval of quiet or lack of activity
senses.example: There was a lull in the fighting over the holiday.

senses.definition: to calm or send to sleep, typically with soothing sounds or movements
senses.example: The rocking of the train lulled her to sleep.

senses.definition: to cause someone to feel deceptively secure or confident
senses.example: The quiet streets lulled them into a false sense of safety.

senses.definition: self-pityingly or tearfully sentimental
senses.example: After a few drinks he grew maudlin about his lost youth.

senses.definition: (of a person) subject to sudden or unpredictable changes of mood or mind
senses.example: The mercurial chef could be charming one minute and furious the next.

senses.definition: a person's ability to cope well with difficulties or to face a demanding situation in a spirited and resilient way
senses.example: The long march tested the soldiers' mettle.

senses.definition: amusement, especially as expressed in laughter
senses.example: His impression of the principal caused great mirth.

senses.definition: liable to change
senses.example: Fashion is a mutable thing.

senses.definition: (typically of an action or activity) wicked or criminal
senses.example: The gang's nefarious activities included smuggling and extortion.

senses.definition: so surprised and confused that one is unsure how to react
senses.example: The question left the candidate nonplussed.

words.note: Nonplussed traditionally means bewildered, not calm or unfazed.

senses.definition: a subtle difference in or shade of meaning, expression or sound
senses.example: The translation misses the nuances of the original.

senses.definition: (of a person or their views) conforming to what is generally or traditionally accepted as right or true
senses.example: Her methods were far from orthodox, but they worked.

senses.definition: to exclude from a society or group
senses.example: She was ostracized by her colleagues for reporting the fraud.

senses.definition: (of a person's face) pale, typically because of poor health
senses.example: He looked pallid after weeks in the hospital.

senses.definition: feeble or insipid
senses.example: The sequel was a pallid imitation of the original.

senses.definition: eager or quick to argue, quarrel or fight
senses.example: The pugnacious senator loved a good fight.

senses.definition: to say that one no longer holds an opinion or belief, especially one considered heretical
senses.example: Under pressure, the scientist recanted his theory.

senses.definition: avoiding the company of other people; solitary
senses.example: The reclusive author never gave interviews.

senses.definition: filled or well supplied with something
senses.example: The book is replete with fascinating detail.

senses.definition: very full of food; sated
senses.example: Replete after the feast, the guests dozed by the fire.

senses.definition: extremely distasteful; unacceptable
senses.example: The idea of eating insects was repugnant to him.

senses.definition: (especially of something undesirable) of common occurrence; widespread
senses.example: Rumors were rife in the office.

senses.definition: full of
senses.example: The essay was rife with errors.

senses.definition: (of a person) reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little
senses.example: The taciturn fisherman spoke only to his dog.

senses.definition: able to be maintained or defended against attack or objection
senses.example: The theory is no longer tenable in light of new evidence.

senses.definition: to prevent someone from accomplishing something
senses.example: The guard thwarted the robbery.

senses.definition: a false, absurd or distorted representation of something
senses.example: The trial was a travesty of justice.

senses.definition: offering nothing that is stimulating or challenging; bland
senses.example: The pop song had vapid lyrics.

senses.definition: keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties
senses.example: Be vigilant about strangers near the school.

senses.definition: a person highly skilled in music or another artistic pursuit
senses.example: The violin virtuoso played without a score.

senses.definition: having or showing a feeling of vague or regretful longing
senses.example: She cast a wistful glance at the old house.
